{"concepts_used":["GC-0097","GC-0040","GC-0156","GC-0153","GC-0046"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part47/1/1/3/2","quote":"The application for an extension of time to file a notice of intention to oppose or a statement of grounds and particulars must be filed with the Trade Marks Office in an approved form and accompanied by the relevant fee (see item 6 in Schedule 9 of the Trade Marks Regulations 1995). The application will not be processed until the fee is paid."},{"ref":"TMM/Part47/1/1/3/2","quote":"A form is available on IP Australia’s website. An opponent is not required to use this form however it may be useful as a guide."},{"ref":"TMM/Part47/1/1/3/2","quote":"The application must be accompanied by a declaration which complies with reg 21.6, setting out the reasons in support of the grounds on which the application is made. If the initial period has expired, the declaration should also include the reason why the application was not made within the period (regs 5.9, 17A.34C)."},{"ref":"TMM/Part47/1/1/3/3","quote":"In granting an extension of time, the Registrar must be satisfied as to the grounds set out in the application and the reasons given in support of those grounds. If the extension application was filed out of time, the Registrar must also be satisfied that there was sufficient reason for the application not being made within time (regs 5.10, 17A.34D)."}],"answer":"To request more time to file a notice of intention to oppose—or a statement of grounds and particulars—the **Manual’s practice** is to lodge:

1. **An extension-of-time application in an approved form**, filed with the Trade Marks Office. IP Australia’s website has a form; the Manual says that particular form is not compulsory, but may be used as a guide. [TMM/Part47/1/1/3/2]
2. **The relevant fee.** The Manual refers to Schedule 9, item 6 of the Regulations and says the request will not be processed until the fee is paid. The supplied passages do not give the fee amount. [TMM/Part47/1/1/3/2]
3. **A declaration complying with regulation 21.6**, explaining the reasons supporting the grounds for your request. Because the deadline has passed, also explain why you did not apply for the extension before the period ended. [TMM/Part47/1/1/3/2]

An extension is not automatic: the Manual says the Registrar must be satisfied about the grounds and supporting reasons and, for a late request, that there was sufficient reason for not applying in time. [TMM/Part47/1/1/3/3]

These are statements of Manual practice, not quotations of legislation. The supplied passages do not set out the available opposition-specific grounds for an extension."}
